/**
   * Indicate that mail is about to be passed to the sink.
   * Once this is called, then the incorporate* methods can be called to pass
   * individual messages.
   * Once delivery is complete, one of endMailDelivery() or abortMailDelivery()
   * must be called.
   *
   * @param uidlDownload ?????
   * @param msgWindow

* Once delivery is complete, one of endMailDelivery() or abortMailDelivery()
   * must be called.
   *
   * @param uidlDownload ?????
   * @param msgWindow
   */
  void beginMailDelivery(in boolean uidlDownload, in nsIMsgWindow msgWindow);

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The current nsIPop3Sink IDL describes beginMailDelivery followed by endMailDelivery or abortMailDelivery, and separate incorporateBegin/write/complete-or-abort calls for each message. beginMailDelivery now has a void IDL result; native failure can still throw through the binding. Its uidlDownload parameter comment remains unexplained. Recommend documenting that distinction when touching this interface; the old public downloadInProgress attribute is absent. This is static source and test-code inspection. Complete Bugzilla and historical review timeline/inline context remain pending. No Thunderbird runtime, build, lint or live accessibility validation ran.
title: Keep the POP3 sink lifecycle explicit in interface documentation
